name: RustCrypto asm-hashes (the sha2 'asm' feature)
baseline: sha2's built-in backends: portable Rust plus SHA-NI and ARMv8 SHA2 intrinsics selected at runtime
verdict_reason: The asm feature was removed in sha2 0.11.0 and the asm-hashes repository is archived. Its maintainers only ever described it as 'a bit faster' than the software backend, and sha2 already uses SHA-NI and ARMv8 SHA2 instructions at runtime, which is where large gains come from.
tier_reason: No published numbers, only a maintainer's qualitative statement.
claimed_speedup: No numbers published; the maintainers say the asm backends 'can be a bit faster than the software backends'.
platforms: x86 and x86_64 Linux, ARM64; Windows x86_64 GNU only (MSVC builds known broken)
one_liner: Assembly SHA-1/SHA-2/MD5 compression functions for RustCrypto; archived and dropped from sha2 0.11 with no published speedup.
how_it_is_fast: Hand-written assembly compression functions based on Project Nayuki's code, built with cc, replaced the portable Rust compression loop when the asm feature was enabled.
use_it_when: Only if you are pinned to sha2 0.10 on a CPU without SHA extensions and have measured a gain yourself
skip_it_when: sha2 0.11 or later: the feature no longer exists
Windows MSVC: builds are known to be broken
CPUs with SHA-NI or ARMv8 SHA2, where sha2 already uses the hardware instructions
caveats: No benchmark numbers were found for the asm backends
tradeoffs: Depends on cc and a C toolchain, with limited cross-platform support per the maintainers

evidence.quote: The asm-hashes backends can be a bit faster than the software backends, but they are a maintenance headache
## NOTE: this repo is in maintenance mode only
Windows MSVC builds are known to be broken.
